extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals and communicators using Prowly to write and publish press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing, structuring, and publishing press releases using the Prowly platform, including content best-practices and Prowly-specific features for creation, scheduling, and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose an angle that matters for your target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important thing to start with is choosing the angle that matters for your target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The angle for a specialist magazine will differ from a local newspaper; write different versions of your release for different audiences. Target not only readers but also journalists—research to avoid targeting the wrong journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target the right journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep in mind that you’re not only targeting potential readers, but also journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don’t do your research and target the wrong journalists, writing good press releases won’t get you anywhere. Use Prowly's recommended contacts feature (right side of Creator) to find contacts suggested based on content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft a catchy headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Your press release needs to have a catchy headline in order to be successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline is the first thing people will read and determines whether they read the whole release. Keep it engaging and relevant to the chosen angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a strong lead with the five W's
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft the lead: introduction or three-sentence summary where impatient readers find answers to the five W’s: what, who, when, where, and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead should quickly communicate the core news and importance so journalists can assess newsworthiness immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide essential details concisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Give your readers the essential details necessary to figure out why this press release is newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t write a novel—briefly explain the important facts and get reporters excited about something they’ll write about. Add any remaining necessary information, but avoid overdoing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include quotes and visuals where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider adding quotes and visuals to make the story more interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes can underline importance or provide human perspective; visuals (images, videos, infographics) can increase engagement—use them to enhance, not replace, text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always include contact details
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t forget to add contact details so journalists will know how to reach you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill out media contact cards (Spokespeople) with all possible fields. If journalists have questions and you omitted contact info, chances of publication are slim.

rubrics_metrics.name: End with a boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: To end a press release, add a boilerplate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boilerplate provides company background for journalists who want to know more about your organization if they read to the end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target press release length (~400 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep in mind that a press release should have somewhere in the neighborhood of 400 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That's roughly one printed page. Slight variance is acceptable, but being significantly shorter or longer typically indicates a problem. Keep everything focused to hit the sweet spot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Press Release Creator preview and autosave
rubrics_metrics.description: At the top of the menu, there's a Preview option and your press releases are automatically saved in Prowly anytime you make a significant change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Preview to check final look before publishing; rely on autosave but also use Save/Save & exit as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage Publication Status correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Change your press release status accordingly by picking Draft, Ready, Schedule, or Published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statuses to indicate progress and to schedule or publish at appropriate times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use publishing visibility options to increase reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing Options: Pin to homepage, Add to slider, Newsroom & tab selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pin to homepage to increase visibility; add to slider to highlight and attract more views; choose newsroom/tab or publish as standalone to control placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configure settings including thumbnail, sharing, and SEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Settings (cogwheel) include configuration options, thumbnail view, sharing settings, and SEO options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill these metadata fields to optimize discoverability and presentation on the newsroom and social shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose fonts for consistent visual style
rubrics_metrics.description: Fonts (Aa icon) - change the typeface to serif or sans-serif in the title, subheadings, and all press release paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a consistent and readable typeface for titles, subheadings and body to maintain professional appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add appropriate attachments in supported formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachments (paperclip) - add any files like documents and images to your press release (available formats: jpg, jpeg, png, svg, tif, tiff, ai, ppt, pptx, odp, doc, docx, odt, rtf, txt, pdf, xls, xlsx, ods, mobi, epub).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach supplemental files journalists may need (press kits, datasheets, images). Ensure correct formats and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide downloadable exports (PDF/DOCX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Download (arrow pointing down icon) - save the prepared press release on your computer in PDF or DOCX format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exports for offline distribution or archiving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage Prowly AI features carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: AI features help generate a press release from ideas, start with a concept, and offer AI reviewing with suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AI to draft or review but validate factual accuracy, tone, and angle before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Prowly's recommended contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: You can view contacts recommended by Prowly based on the content of your press release on the right side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider these recommendations to improve targeting; still verify fit and relevance to your angle and media list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate content elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic elements: Text, Header & Sub header, Lead, Ordered & Unordered lists, Quote, Annotation, Table, Divider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use headers to divide thematic sections; lead for intro/summary; lists to enumerate benefits; quotes for emphasis; tables for data; dividers to segment content. You can turn any text element into another type and reorganize as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use design elements thoughtfully
rubrics_metrics.description: Design elements: Image, Gallery, Full-width image, Full-width video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images between paragraphs add color; use graphics/infographics; galleries for multiple images (slider or side-by-side). Full-width images can include a description up to 180 characters; full-width videos should be high quality/resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strike a balance between images and text
rubrics_metrics.description: Although images are great to include in your press release, don’t get carried away and make it all photos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit number of pictures if photos aren’t essential. Think quality, not quantity; avoid overpowering your text with visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed external integrations when useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrations: Custom link, Facebook post, Tweet, Instagram post (public account required), LinkedIn post, YouTube, Vimeo, SlideShare, Prezi, GIF by Giphy, previously published Prowly press releases, Custom code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed social posts, videos, slideshows or custom code to enrich the story; ensure public visibility (e.g., public Instagram) and relevance to content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill building blocks: Authors and Spokespeople
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors - card showing photo and contact details; Spokespeople - contact card for media inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you add more than one author only the first is visible on main page; fill all possible fields in media contact cards so journalists know who to contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Call-to-Action buttons effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Call-to-Action Button - persuade people to click with some convincing phrase and direct them with a link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear, action-oriented phrase and link to relevant landing pages to drive engagement or conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reorganize and edit content post-publishing if needed
rubrics_metrics.description: You can always change the type of any text element and reorganize everything easily—even after you’ve published or sent out your press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor performance and make adjustments to improve engagement; updates can be made to optimize content that’s underperforming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule and backdate publications with correct timezone
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose Scheduled status, define date, time, and timezone, and confirm to publish at desired time. You can also schedule a publication with a backdate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scheduling to publish at optimal times; backdating is useful when migrating multiple press releases from another site or offline resources—set a past date to give the press release Published status.
